name: Orange County
dept_sa: Colin Seaman (listed as Interim State's Attorney)

states-attorney.note_extra: Mid-term change: the 2022 winner, Dickson Corbett, no longer holds the office; the Department page lists Colin Seaman as Interim State's Attorney (see county notes).

sheriff.final_note: The figures recorded here are the final recount figures. The Elections Database contest page carries the canvass figures (Contois 6,603; Bohnyak 6,503; write-ins 20). Bohnyak petitioned for a recount; the recount, completed November 28, 2022 and certified by the Superior Court the following day, added three votes to Contois and removed three from Bohnyak, for a final tally of 6,606 to 6,500 (White River Valley Herald, 'Recount Confirms Contois Is Winner'). The Secretary of State's results index lists this race among the 2022 general election recounts.

extra_sources.note: The White River Valley Herald, 'Recount Confirms Contois Is Winner' (November/December 2022): the recount expanded George Contois's lead to a final tally of 6,606 to 6,500 over incumbent Sheriff Bill Bohnyak; Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Mann certified the results on November 29, 2022.

high-bailiff.final_note: The Elections Database names no candidate for this contest. Two write-in campaigns were waged for the seat (Chris Helali of Vershire and Tom Harty of Randolph); the state Canvassing Committee certified Helali the winner with 446 votes, as reported by The White River Valley Herald ('Helali Wins High Bailiff As Write-In', November 14, 2024, citing the official certification) and confirmed in Seven Days' 2026 retrospective. No party label attaches to a write-in candidacy.

extra_sources.note: Seven Days (2026), 'High Bailiff Position Is in the Spotlight This Campaign Season': Chris Helali won the 2024 Orange County high bailiff election by earning 446 votes through a write-in campaign.
The White River Valley Herald (2025): Christopher Helali was elected high bailiff in Orange County in November 2024 as a write-in candidate and holds the office.

sa_transition.event: appointed a Superior Court judge in 2023 (he had himself been appointed SA in April 2021 and won election in 2022)

sources.note: White River Valley Herald (2023), reporting Governor Scott's appointments: Colin Seaman was appointed Orange County State's Attorney replacing H. Dickson Corbett, who was appointed a Superior Court judge; Seaman serves until February 1, 2027. The Governor's office announced the appointment on September 8, 2023.

Department of State's Attorneys and Sheriffs, Orange County office page: lists Colin Seaman as the office's State's Attorney (styled 'Interim State's Attorney' in its staff list) as of the October 2026 retrieval.
